αἰνέω: (to tell;) to praise, approve, acquiesce in
βακχεύω: to keep the feast of Bacchus, celebrate his mysteries
βλέπω: to see, have the power of sight
γιγνώσκω: to learn to know, to perceive, mark, learn
δειμαίνω: to be afraid, in a fright
διαιρέω: to take one from another, to cleave in twain, to divide into parts
εἰσοράω: to look into, look upon, view, behold
εὐτυχέω: to be well off, successful, prosperous
θεσπίζω: to declare by oracle, prophesy, divine
καθίζω: to cause to sit down; to sit down
καραδοκέω: to watch eagerly, anxiously (for the outcome)
κατάγω: to lead down; bring back (from exile)
κενοταφέω: to honour with an empty tomb
κινέω: to set in motion, to move
κλίνω: to make to bend, slope; recline
κρίνω: to pick out, choose, judge, determine
λέγω: to say, tell, speak; epic and arch.: pick, gather
λεηλατέω: to drive away cattle as booty, to make booty
μέλλω: to think of doing, intend to do, to be about to do
μένω: to stay at home, stay where one is, not stir
μαρτυρέω: to be a witness, to bear witness, give evidence, bear testimony
μεταίρω: to lift up and remove, to shift
μεταβάλλω: to throw into a different position, to turn quickly
μοχθέω: to be weary with toil, to be sore distressed
μυθεύω: to speak of, to relate fabulously
νοσέω: to be sick, ill, to ail
οἰκτίρω: to pity, feel pity for, have pity upon
πάλλω: to poise, shake, sway, leap, cast lots
πελάζω: to approach, come near, draw near
περάω: to drive right through; pass, penetrate
πορεύω: to make to go, carry, convey
πορθμεύω: to carry over (a body of water)
πρεσβεύω: to be the elder; to be an ambassador
προβαίνω: to step on, step forward, advance
προστίθημι: to add, to apply, to close (a door); mid. to join (a group), take as an ally
προτίθημι: to place before, to propose, to prefer
σείω: to shake, move to and fro
σπαργάω: to be full to bursting, to swell, be ripe
σπεύδω: to set a-going, to urge on, hasten, quicken
στρατηλατέω: to lead an army into the field
συντήκω: to fuse into one mass, to weld together
συσκιάζω: to shade quite over, throw a shade over, shade closely
σύνειμι: be with (incl. be wife of, study with)
τιμάω: to honor; to value something at a price (gen.)
τιμωρέω: to seek, exact vengeance; help to retaliate
τλάω: to take upon oneself, to bear, suffer, undergo
τυγχάνω: (with gen.) to hit the mark, to get; (with pple) to happen to, to actually
φαίνω: to bring to light, make to appear
φεύγω: to flee, take flight, run away
φιλοψυχέω: to love one’s life: to be cowardly
φρονέω: to think, to have understanding, to be sage, wise, prudent
φυλάσσω: to keep watch and ward, keep guard
χαίρω: to rejoice, be glad, be delighted
χρῄζω: to need, want, lack, have need of
ἀίσσω: to move with a quick shooting motion, to shoot, dart, glance
ἀξιόω: to think worthy of; to expect
ἀρκέω: to ward off; to be sufficient
ἀτίζω: not to honour, to hold in no honour
ἐκλείπω: to leave out, omit, pass over
ἐκλύω: to loose, release, set free, from
ἐκτρέφω: to bring up from childhood, rear up
ἐξαμαρτάνω: to err from the mark, fail
ἐπαίρω: to lift up and set on
ἐπισκήπτω: to make to lean upon, make a (deathbed) request, denounce (for perjury)
ἐράω: to love, to be in love with
ἐρεθίζω: to rouse to anger, rouse to fight, irritate
ἔξεστι: it is allowed, it is in one’s power, is possible
ἔχω: have, hold; be able; (+ adv.) be; (mid.) cling to, be next to (+ gen.)
ἱστουργέω: to work at the loom, weave
ἵημι: to set a going, put in motion
ὑπερβάλλω: to throw over; outdo, surpass, postpone
ὑπερφέρω: to bear or carry over, transfer; to surpass, excel
ὠφελέω: to help, aid, assist, to be of use
